blocks.text: The chapter places several limits on human control beside one another: speech and vows before God require restraint and reverence (vv. 1-7); oppression can persist within layers of authority (vv. 8-9); and wealth cannot secure lasting advantage, since it may bring anxiety, vanish, and cannot be carried away at death (vv. 10-17). Its closing words do not deny these limits. Instead, they describe eating, drinking, enjoying one’s work, and rejoicing in one’s portion as gifts enabled by God rather than as possessions humans can finally master.
